clue.text: All the cards? One of them is limiting North on board game

parts.note: a deck is a complete pack of playing cards

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the two words around it close in on the compass point

parts.note: a ten is one card in the pack
taken as written

explanation.surface: A card player at a board game holds the whole pack and wonders about one card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' means the card and 'is' enclose the compass point. 'On board' is the ship's deck, where this quoits-style game is played, not a board game like chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck tennis is a game with a ring of rope tossed over a net, played aboard ship, hence on board.

clue.text: Confound ostentation — and blow Mark!

definitions.meaning: a mild oath: '... it!' means much the same as 'confound it!'
... in the sense of showy style or flair
a ... is a sudden striking blow, as in ... against rocks
a punctuation mark, the horizontal line used in writing

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation at someone's showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the four clue words is a separate dictionary sense of one short word: an oath, flair, a strike and a punctuation sign.

clue.text: Praise 50% of Mr Men in jest

indicators.note: in tells us the two pieces before it go inside the word for jest

parts.note: to cod is to joke or hoax

indicators.note: 50% of a two-letter word is just its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Admiring the children's Mr Men books in a light-hearted way.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' takes the first half of 'Mr'; 'in' puts it plus 'Men' inside the joke word. 'Mr Men' are children's picture books, but here they split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend someone is to praise them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Unwisely lose the essential element: b—– hot tub — what that wee, airworthy Beth's showing off!

indicators.note: showing off suggests the letters strutting about, so these words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the initial letter B with a coy dash is fodder as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the possessive adds no letter, giving the four letters of the name

explanation.surface: A rude exclamation about a hot tub and a girl called Beth showing off in it.
explanation.walkthrough: All the words from 'b' to 'Beth's' (31 letters) are rearranged. 'wee' in the surface hints at bodily functions in the tub, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means discarding something valuable along with what is unwanted, so foolishly losing what matters most.

clue.text: In love, badly beat Mark!

indicators.note: In placed first signals the jumbled letters go inside the word for love

parts.note: love in a score means nothing, which is none

indicators.note: badly means the letters of beat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hopelessly in love has been badly beaten, and we are told to take note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts the anagram of the fodder (from 'badly') inside the word for nothing; love is zero in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Nota bene is the Latin instruction to note well, used to call attention to something, as 'mark!' does.

clue.text: Send to Coventry, funny region

indicators.note: funny means peculiar or odd, so the letters of region are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: Shunning someone for coming from a funny part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them; Coventry is an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: To send to Coventry is to ostracise someone, deliberately taking no notice of them.

clue.text: Heavily strike driver?

definitions.meaning: to beat hard with a heavy stick
a driver is a golf stick used for long shots from the tee

explanation.surface: Hit hard by a motorist?
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel blow is a verb sense, and a golfer's driver is one of the sticks in the bag.

clue.text: A letter to Greek includes a measure of Latin

indicators.note: includes signals the single letter goes inside the Greek letter

parts.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, a letter to a Greek
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note to a Greek correspondent contains some Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'measure' is a dance, not a unit, and 'Latin' means Latin American.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a lively Brazilian dance, so a measure (a dance) of Latin American origin.

clue.text: Black-shoed shuffle for group of 19

indicators.note: a shuffle is a dance step and a mixing of cards, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dance routine performed in black shoes by a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is IAN DURY, the singer whose band was the Blockheads.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blockheads were the band backing singer Ian Dury, the answer to 19-down.

clue.text: Beelzebub's accepting time of celebration for Welsh listeners

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the date goes inside the devil's name

parts.note: Beelzebub is another name for Satan, and the possessive supplies the final S
1 March is St David's Day, the Welsh national day, written MAR I

explanation.surface: The devil welcomes a Welsh festival for the benefit of a radio audience.
explanation.walkthrough: MAR I is 1st March, St David's Day; St David is the patron saint of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samaritans are a British charity whose volunteers listen to people in distress.

clue.text: Military 'supplies' (in inverted commas)

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, so in a down-reading sense the letters run backwards
in shows the letters are found inside the following word

explanation.surface: Putting quotation marks round a military word to show it is a euphemism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted commas' looks like quotation marks; 'in' takes OMMA from 'commas' and 'inverted' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is short for ammunition, the military supplies of bullets and shells.

clue.text: See 3
Catcall from writer that hurt!

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
ow is the cry of pain

explanation.surface: A writer cries out at a jeer from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catcall' is a jeer in the surface but literally the call of a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's call is the sound it makes, a mew, the literal reading of catcall.

clue.text: Distinguishing feature making Spooner cry with laughter?

indicators.note: naming Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: mirth is merriment and laughter
a bark is a sharp cry, as of a dog

explanation.surface: A distinguishing feature that makes someone cry with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Mirth bark becomes the answer once the first letters are swapped. The Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping word sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark on the skin from birth is a distinguishing feature used to identify someone.

clue.text: I'll stop you from lying about the rust — it's odd

indicators.note: about means around or in disarray, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: rum means odd or strange in British slang

explanation.surface: A remark that something strange is going on with the rust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges THE RUST into TRUTHSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A truth serum is a drug said to compel a person to tell the truth, so it stops them lying.

clue.text: Bird from Liverpool getting engaged to Marvin

parts.note: Liverpool football club are nicknamed the Reds
Hank Marvin is the guitarist of the Shadows

explanation.surface: A gossip item about someone from Liverpool getting engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Hank Marvin was lead guitarist of the British band the Shadows; Liverpool FC play in red.
explanation.definitionFit: The redshank is a wading bird with red legs.

clue.text: Well-lit sailor wants to do no work

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
to laze is to idle

explanation.surface: A drunk sailor wants a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-lit' looks like slang for drunk, but it means burning brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ablaze is on fire and so brightly lit.

clue.text: On half a drum with one digit, play 'The Little General'

indicators.note: half a word made of two identical halves leaves one of them

parts.note: a tom-tom is a drum played with the hands
the thumb is one of the hand's digits

explanation.surface: A drummer plays a tune about a small military leader.
explanation.walkthrough: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of the tiny P T Barnum performer Charles Stratton.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage title of Barnum's famously small performer was General Tom Thumb.

clue.text: Showing outward strain, I left book and hat

indicators.note: showing on the outside means the word for strain wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to try is to strain or attempt
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone under visible stress walks off leaving a book and a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing outward' puts TRY round I, L and B.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with a dented crown.

clue.text: Victim of rhythm stick could arrange to ruin day

indicators.note: could arrange signals the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A drummer's victim plans to spoil the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Dury's hit 'Hit Me With Your Rhythm Stick' makes the singer the one being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer of 'Hit Me With Your Rhythm Stick' asks to be struck, so he is its victim.

clue.text: Cooked hot Latin grub without getting a grip

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word for grub goes around the rest

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: cooked means altered or prepared, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe for hot Latin food made without any grip on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: the grub word goes round the cooked letters plus the Latin abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A foothold is a secure place for the foot, hence a grip in climbing.

clue.text: See 3
Aged prophet tucking into South American snack

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the prophet sits within the abbreviation

parts.note: Amos was an Old Testament prophet, hence aged

explanation.surface: An old seer eating a snack from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating but means placing inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried pastry filled with spiced vegetables or meat, eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Those starting sprint badly, after all, finish under high pressure

parts.note: the starting letters of sprint and badly are S and B, written S and B
at last means after all, finally

explanation.surface: Runners who start poorly finish strongly under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those starting' gives the initials of 'sprint' and 'badly', joined by the word 'and': S AND B.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandblasting gives a surface finish by firing sand at it under high pressure.

clue.text: In the company of women, it's hard

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A remark that it is hard to be among women.
explanation.definitionFit: With means accompanied by, as in going somewhere with friends.

clue.text: A bit much — a pregnant bloke!

indicators.note: a bit of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A pregnant man is a bit much to believe.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap and bloke are both informal British words for a man.

clue.text: Tin chucked by regular debauchee

indicators.note: chucked by means thrown out of, so the word for tin is removed from the word for regular

parts.note: routine means regular or usual
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rake throws away a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN comes out of the middle of ROUTINE leaving ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A roue is a dissolute man given to debauchery.

clue.text: Company time engaged in quiet manoeuvring with mum, flirting

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so the time letter sits inside the jumbled word
manoeuvring means moving around, so the letters of quiet are rearranged

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A flirtatious woman with her mother at a quiet company function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' turns QUIET into QUETI, and 'engaged in' puts T inside it: QUETTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Coquettish means behaving flirtatiously.

clue.text: Irish county spread

definitions.meaning: a county in the west of Ireland
short for mayonnaise, a sandwich spread

explanation.surface: An Irish county known for a spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county of Connacht, and mayo is the casual short form of mayonnaise.

clue.text: Fleet Street source of legendary piemeat, herbs or nuts filling roll

definitions.text: Fleet Street source of legendary piemeat

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the jumbled letters go into the bread roll

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pie of herbs or nuts in a roll from a Fleet Street shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd, the legendary demon barber of Fleet Street, turned his victims into pie filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeney Todd's barbershop in Fleet Street supplied the meat for Mrs Lovett's pies in the legend.
